root_cause.text: The driver failed to explicitly free generic IRQ chips allocated during probe when removing the IRQ domain, because the domain flags did not include `IRQ_DOMAIN_FLAG_DESTROY_GC`, causing a resource leak and potential use-after-free from stale entries on the global `gc_list`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `irq_domain_remove_generic_chips(bank->domain)` before `irq_domain_remove(bank->domain)` in `rockchip_gpio_remove()`. The commit message states that generic chips are leaked and remain on `gc_list` after driver removal, leading to possible use-after-free during suspend/resume/shutdown callbacks.

candidates.rationale: The irq_domain_remove call directly triggers removal of the IRQ domain without first freeing the generic IRQ chips, leading to resource leak and potential use-after-free from stale entries on the global gc_list. The missing call to remove generic IRQ chips is the direct cause of the vulnerability.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement removes the IRQ domain without first freeing the generic IRQ chips allocated during probe. Because the domain flags did not include IRQ_DOMAIN_FLAG_DESTROY_GC, the generic chip resources are not automatically freed, leading to a resource leak and potential use-after-free from stale entries on the global gc_list.
